item.description: The increasing accessibility of generative artificial intelligence has enabled individuals to integrate sophisticated computational capabilities into everyday intellectual activities. item.title: YR-MPE: a modular desktop platform for agent-operable and reproducible phylogenetic workflows
item.description: Abstract Phylogenomic analyses combine many tools, file formats and execution modes. Desktop graphical user interfaces make individual steps accessible but hide their state from scripts; command-line pipelines make steps scriptable but leave parameter discovery, provenance and recovery to the user; and emerging LLM agents can call command-line tools but cannot inspect a GUI session or its artifacts. item.title: HAMU: Autonomy Without Sovereignty — Cognition, Continuity, and Authority in Persistent AI Systems
item.description: HAMU (HOST-AWARE MEDIATION UNIT) is a conceptual architecture for hosting persistent artificial intelligence (AI) agents that can carry out assignments, check their work, and correct mistakes. Plans and results can outlast the permissions that governed the original task. item.title: Spectra-Scope: a toolkit for automated and interpretable characterization of material properties from spectral data
item.description: Spectroscopy is a central pillar of materials characterization, providing useful information on properties like structure, composition, or excited state dynamics of a system. However, many spectroscopic techniques present challenges in the development of interpretable, performant, and reliable supervised learning models due to the wide range of possible nonlinear correlations that can exist between the signal and the response variable (target) of interest. item.title: An AI-Driven, Workflow-Aware Virtual Customer Support Assistant for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
item.description: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that sell through messaging platforms often handle customer enquiries manually, leading to fragmented conversations, delayed responses and inconsistent service. This article proposes a workflow-aware conversational support assistant that combines a large language model (LLM), retrieval grounding, merchant API tools and context-preserving human hand-off. item.title: “Should I Give Up Now?” Investigating LLM Pitfalls in Software Engineering
item.description: Software engineers are increasingly incorporating AI assistants into their workflows to enhance productivity and alleviate cognitive load. However, experiences with Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT vary widely. While some engineers find them useful, others deem them counterproductive due to inaccuracies in their responses. item.title: Can GenAI numeracy tutors support self-regulated learning?
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has been the focus of much attention in the higher education sector, both for its potential to support personalised and adaptive learning, but also due to the risk that students may outsource learning to it, leading to gaps in their professional or discipline competencies. item.description: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. item.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: When Human Assurance Matters: Task Complexity and Pre-Interaction Expected Satisfaction in Human-AI Hybrid Service Systems
item.description: Consumers frequently disengage from AI service encounters because they doubt whether chatbots can resolve their requests. Although human–AI hybrid systems provide human backup, this capability is often concealed. item.title: Within-Host Infection Dynamics
item.description: This dissertation presents a rigorous mathematical study of within-host infection dynamics through the development and analysis of nonlinear differential equation models. The work is motivated by the need to understand the complex interactions between pathogens and host cells, accounting for mechanisms such as saturation in infection, cellular quiescence, immune-mediated control, and cooperative bacterial growth. item.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder: pathogenesis, epidemiological characteristics, animal models, and potential therapeutic strategies
item.description: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a complex neurobehavioral disorder that disproportionately affects military service members. The clinical presentation of PTSD is heterogeneous and may overlap with other psychiatric conditions. item.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
item.description: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge. We aim to investigate if Test-Driven Development (TDD) can improve the quality of code generated by an LLM in a fully autonomous context, within a pilot project at Decerno AB. item.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
item.description: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. item.title: Lived experiences of relationships to generative AI mental health chatbots among adults
item.description: Abstract Background Nigeria's mental health system serves less than 10% of those in need, with severe provider shortages and deep-seated stigma.
